title: WHY GOD HATES GOSSIP
paragraphs:
WHY GOD HATES GOSSIP
The Sin Most Christians Excuse... Until It Destroys Someone They Love
You have probably never seen a church split because someone robbed a bank.
You have probably never watched a family collapse because someone committed armed robbery during Sunday service.
You have probably never seen lifelong friendships destroyed because someone publicly worshiped an idol in the middle of the sanctuary.
But gossip?
Gossip has shattered churches.
Gossip has broken marriages.
Gossip has divided families.
Gossip has crushed reputations.
Gossip has driven wounded people away from the very places where they were supposed to find healing.
And what makes it even more dangerous is that gossip rarely looks evil when it begins.
It often sounds like concern.
It disguises itself as prayer requests.
It hides behind phrases like, “I think you should know…”
“Just between us…”
“Don't tell anyone I told you…”
“I'm only saying this because I care…”
Yet God sees beyond the disguise.
He sees what is happening in the heart.
And Scripture reveals something deeply sobering:
God does not merely dislike gossip.
God hates it.
That statement makes many people uncomfortable.
We like talking about God's love.
We celebrate God's mercy.
We rejoice in His grace.
And rightly so.
But if we truly love God, we must also care about what He hates.
One of the strongest passages in Scripture appears in Proverbs 6:16-19:
"There are six things that the LORD hates, seven that are an abomination to him..."
Among them is:
"...a false witness who breathes out lies, and one who sows discord among brothers."

The Hebrew word used for "sows discord" is מְשַׁלֵּחַ מְדָנִים (meshalleach medanim), carrying the idea of deliberately scattering conflict, spreading division, and planting seeds of strife among people.
God calls it an abomination.
Not an inconvenience.
Not a personality flaw.
An abomination.
Think about that.
The same God who stretched out the heavens.
The same God who formed the oceans.
The same God who sent His Son to die for sinners.
Looks at gossip and calls it detestable.
Why?
Because gossip attacks something precious to Him.
People.
Every person bears the image of God.
Genesis 1:27 declares:
"So God created man in his own image."
Every rumor whispered behind someone's back is aimed at someone God created.
Every reputation damaged belongs to someone Christ died to save.
Every careless conversation has the potential to wound a soul that Jesus loves.
That changes everything.
The problem with gossip is that it often feels harmless to the speaker while being devastating to the victim.
A person may laugh after sharing a juicy story.
Meanwhile, the target of that story loses friendships, opportunities, trust, peace, and sometimes even their faith community.
Words leave scars.
Scripture repeatedly warns us about their power.
Proverbs 18:21 says:
"Death and life are in the power of the tongue."
Not swords.
Not armies.
Not governments.
The tongue.
A few ounces of muscle inside the mouth possess the power to breathe life into people or slowly destroy them.
The New Testament intensifies this warning.
James writes:
The Greek text says:
ἡ γλῶσσα πῦρ (hē glōssa pyr)
"The tongue is fire."
Not merely like fire.
Fire itself.
One careless spark can burn down an entire forest.
One careless sentence can burn down an entire community.
Many believers spend years praying for revival while simultaneously participating in the very behavior that extinguishes it.
Revival requires unity.
Gossip creates division.
Revival requires humility.
Gossip feeds pride.
Revival requires truth.
Gossip often survives on assumptions.
This is why Satan loves gossip.
Because gossip allows him to destroy people without ever touching them.
The enemy simply whispers.
Someone repeats it.
Someone else expands it.
Another person believes it.
Soon the damage becomes irreversible.
The original story may not even resemble the truth anymore.
And yet lives have already been affected.
This pattern is ancient.
In fact, one could argue that the first gossip in human history happened in Eden.
The serpent approached Eve and subtly questioned God's character.
"Did God actually say...?"
Genesis 3:1
The enemy planted suspicion.
He distorted truth.
He poisoned trust.
Every act of gossip follows the same pattern.
Suspicion.
Distortion.
Division.
That is why gossip feels so spiritually dark.
Its DNA resembles the tactics of the serpent.
Jesus described Satan in John 8:44:
"When he lies, he speaks out of his own character."
Gossip often partners with lies, exaggerations, assumptions, half-truths, and selective storytelling.
It becomes a tool that accomplishes the enemy's purposes while convincing us we are serving righteous ones.
Perhaps that is why so many Christians struggle to recognize it.
We easily identify obvious sins.
Drunkenness.
Adultery.
Theft.
Violence.
But gossip often receives a free pass.
Entire conversations revolve around discussing people who are not present.
Entire social circles are built around mutual criticism.
Entire online communities survive by dissecting the failures of others.
And all the while, believers convince themselves they are simply sharing information.
Yet Jesus never called us to be distributors of people's failures.
He called us to be ambassadors of reconciliation.
There is another reason God hates gossip.
It reveals something hidden inside us.
Often gossip is not primarily about the person being discussed.
It is about the heart of the person speaking.
Gossip frequently emerges from jealousy.
Bitterness.
Insecurity.
Pride.
Resentment.
A desire to feel superior.
A need for attention.
The mouth reveals what the heart contains.
Jesus said:
"Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks."
Matthew 12:34
The Greek phrase is:
ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ περισσεύματος τῆς καρδίας λαλεῖ τὸ στόμα
"For out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks."
If destructive words constantly emerge from our lips, God is inviting us to examine something deeper than our speech.
He is inviting us to examine our hearts.
And this is where the Gospel becomes incredibly beautiful.
Because this article is not ultimately about gossip.
It is about grace.
It is about what Jesus does with sinners.
Every one of us has failed.
Every one of us has spoken words we regret.
Every one of us has participated in conversations that dishonored God.
Some of us have been wounded by gossip.
Others have wounded people through gossip.
Many of us have done both.
The scandal is real.
But grace is greater.
At the cross, Jesus carried not only our visible sins but also our hidden ones.
The careless conversations.
The secret whispers.
The reputations we damaged.
The words we cannot take back.
Isaiah 53:5 says:
"But he was pierced for our transgressions."
The Hebrew word for transgressions is פֶּשַׁע (pesha), referring to rebellion against God.
Christ died for those sins too.
Not just the dramatic scandals.
Not just the public failures.
The private conversations nobody else knows about.
The Gospel declares that forgiveness is available.
Transformation is possible.
The tongue that once spread destruction can become an instrument of healing.
The mouth that once spread rumors can proclaim the Gospel.
The person who once caused division can become a peacemaker.
That is what Jesus does.
He rewrites stories.
He takes scandal and turns it into grace.
He takes broken people and turns them into testimonies.
He takes sinners and makes them saints.
Perhaps as you read this, the Holy Spirit has brought someone to mind.
Someone you spoke about.
Someone you judged unfairly.
Someone whose reputation suffered because of your words.
Do not ignore that conviction.
Conviction is not condemnation.
Conviction is God's invitation back to Himself.
Repent.
Seek forgiveness where possible.
Choose truth.
Choose love.
Choose silence when silence honors God.
Choose encouragement when criticism feels easier.
And if you have been the victim of gossip, hear this clearly:
God sees every lie.
God hears every whisper.
God knows every injustice.
Your identity was never determined by the rumors people spread about you.
Your identity is determined by the One who died for you and rose again.
Jesus knows the truth.
And His verdict matters infinitely more than public opinion.
Maybe that is why gossip is so tragic.
It attempts to write someone's story without permission.
But only Jesus has that authority.
Only Jesus knows the full story.
Only Jesus sees every wound, every battle, every tear, every failure, and every victory.
And only Jesus can rewrite everything.
So before you share that story.
Before you repeat that rumor.
Before you pass along information that does not belong to you—
Ask yourself one question:
Will this glorify Christ?
If the answer is no, let it die with you.
The world already has enough critics.
What it desperately needs are followers of Jesus whose words sound like their Savior.
Your honesty may encourage someone else who is fighting the same battle.
The rumors people spread may follow you for a season, but the grace of Jesus follows you forever.
